subject: CAIQ SDLC request — delivery of code review excerpts, CI trigger logs, and deviation summary
messages:
From: security@finledger.com
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 11 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CAIQ follow-up — SDLC artifacts requested

Jonas,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. As part of FinLedger's CAIQ scoping we need a compact set of SDLC artifacts we can ingest into our assessment tool: short code review excerpts showing reviewer identities and timestamps, a slice of CI trigger logs around merges to main (last 90 days), and any documented deviations/approval traces when a code change bypassed normal gates.

A few constraints: we need CSV or PDF outputs (zipped if multiple), and a short plain-text deviation summary that maps exceptions to JIRA/PR numbers. Can you confirm what you can deliver and an ETA?

Thanks,
Lina Ortega
Security Lead — FinLedger
security@finledger.com

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: security@finledger.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 11 Mar 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CAIQ follow-up — SDLC artifacts requested

Lina,

Appreciate the clear list. We can provide the items you described. Proposed plan: 

1) Code review excerpts: we'll pull 2–3 representative PRs per service for the last 90 days, redacting any unrelated proprietary diffs and including reviewer names, timestamps, and approval comments.
2) CI trigger slice: export of trigger events (merge/force-merge/auto-merge) with build IDs and timestamp.
3) Deviation summary: a short PDF that maps each exception to the internal change ticket/approval artifact.

ETA: initial package by Mon PDT (2028-03-13) if that works. Kimberly will run the export and Marissa will validate redactions and approval traces.

I'll also put an access-only Drive folder link in the next message for the actual files. If you need signed attestations for any item, let me know.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Director, Trust & Security (on behalf of Compliance)
Redwood Inference

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com
To: security@finledger.com
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 13 Mar 2028 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: SDLC exports: code review excerpts + CI triggers (encrypted attachments)

Hi Lina — attaching the exports per Jonas's plan. Attachments (zipped):
- code_review_excerpt_batchA.zip — contains JSONL of PR metadata (id, title, author, reviewer, review_time, approval_flag) for 35 PRs across runtime/service stacks; diffs redacted to 'REDACTED' where necessary.
- ci-trigger-events-2028-03.csv — slice of CI trigger events (timestamp, branch, actor, trigger_type, build_id).
- deviation_approvals_2028-03.pdf — formal trace showing where a change took an exception path (ticket ids, approver signatures, and time).

Notes:
- We removed any personally identifiable customer data.
- For PRs marked 'security-exception' there is an explicit approval entry; where approvals were done via emergency channel, we've linked to the approval ticket in the PDF (internal JIRA links).
- Files are encrypted with password: we sent that to FinLedger's key recipient via your secure channel (per your request).

Drive link (view-only): https://drive.redwood.com/FinLedger/CAIQ/2028-sdlc/ (access granted to security@finledger.com)

If you need different file formats or a larger sample, flag it and we can widen the export.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr Manager, Security Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: auditor@cloudassure.com
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, security@finledger.com
Cc: devops@finledger.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 13 Mar 2028 11:35:00 -0700
Subject: RE: SDLC exports: quick follow-up on deviation evidence

Jonas / Lina — thanks for the files, Kimberly. Quick follow-up request from the audit team: for two deviation cases in the PDF (JIRA-4872 and JIRA-5011) we need the merge commit SHA and the CI job logs for the failing/stressed step that prompted the emergency approval. We only need the build logs for those jobs (redacted of secrets/keys). Can Redwood provide the job stdout/stderr snippets and the merge commit id for each?

Also, can you confirm whether the emergency approvals were captured in the change management system (ticket comment thread) or only in Slack approvals? If Slack, we will need an exported timestamped message thread or an attestation explaining why the change management entry is the primary record.

Best,
Aaron Patel
Senior Auditor — CloudAssure Audits

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: auditor@cloudassure.com, security@finledger.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 13 Mar 2028 15:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RE: SDLC exports: quick follow-up on deviation evidence

Aaron — thanks for the clarity. Action items and what we'll deliver by EOD: 

- For JIRA-4872 and JIRA-5011: we'll extract the merge commit SHAs (sha1s) and export the CI job logs for the specific failing steps. Sensitive tokens are already redacted in logs; we'll further redact any IP addresses that FinLedger requests.
- Slack approvals: these were an emergency flow for JIRA-5011 only; the approval is recorded both in Slack and in a follow-up ticket comment (search key: JIRA-5011-approval). We'll export the Slack thread as an HTML/text snippet and include an attestation PDF signed by the change owner stating the primary record locations.
- We'll attach the two job log snippets as plain text and include a short mapping table (PR -> commit SHA -> build_id -> approval artifact).

Kimberly and Marissa will assemble the artifacts. Grace will be the point-on verification for the exported logs. 

If you want the raw logs directly in the Drive folder, confirm and we'll drop them there with restricted access.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Director, Trust & Security
Redwood Inference
